planting.note: Plant bare-root or container shrubs in early spring; Polar Jewel is self-infertile and needs a genetically distinct, overlapping-bloom pollinizer such as Aurora, Berry Blue, Indigo Treat, or Indigo Gem planted nearby for good fruit set.

directions: Plant in well-drained loam or sandy loam in full sun alongside a compatible pollinizer, since Polar Jewel is self-infertile and will not crop well alone. A vigorous Russian-bred haskap selection, it produces large, elongated, dark blue berries with powdery bloom in an early-to-mid bloom group, ripening to a sweet flavor often described as a cross between blueberry and raspberry, good for fresh eating, jam, jelly, and baking. The upright, rounded bush reaches roughly 4 to 5 feet tall and wide at maturity and is extremely cold-hardy, tolerating winter lows well below -40F, but like all haskaps it struggles in hot, humid summer climates and is a poor fit for Gulf Coast gardens. Prune only to remove dead or crossing wood for the first several years, then begin renewal pruning of the oldest canes once mature to sustain fruit production.
